levels.L1: Unit — pure Python logic in the API (e.g. onion/URL routing). No VM, no network, no app. Runs in milliseconds.
levels.L2: Integration — a real NixOS backend boots in a VM and its routing is checked over a transport. No app involved.
levels.L3: App usage — the SelfPrivacy app is driven like a user (open, navigate tabs, add a service, ...) against a running backend, and screen-recorded.
levels.install: Install — provision a backend onto a device/VM via one setup (diagram Install + Network), then verify it landed. Network-independent.
levels.reach: Reach — make an installed box reachable for friends via one route of the setup diagram (Reach + Name): the route's apply step, run on the box over SSH.

setup_map.doc: The matrix axes ARE the setup diagram's toggles (docs/diagrams/setup-map.json meta.toggles): setup (--on) = Install+Network, reach row (--reach/--name) = Reach+Name. `./dash setups` checks they still match the diagram.

methods.label: LAN cable
methods.desc: Netboot the server over a direct LAN cable from your computer (router out of the path), then install with nixos-anywhere.

methods.label: Wifi
methods.desc: Your computer is on router R's wifi; the server netboots THROUGH R (needs R configured for network boot).

methods.label: USB stick
methods.desc: Boot the server from an installer USB stick and install to its internal disk (no link to your computer).

methods.label: VM
methods.desc: The server is a VirtualBox VM on your own computer (build-and-run.sh). No cable, no router.

nets.label: cable→R
nets.desc: the server's LAN cable goes into your router R (internet via the cable); no wifi

nets.label: cable+wifi→R
nets.desc: cable into R, plus a wifi config for the SAME router R

nets.label: wifi-only
nets.desc: no cable: the server runs on wifi only (wifi that reaches the internet)

nets.label: cable→R, wifi→Y
nets.desc: cable into R, plus a wifi config for ANOTHER router Y

reaches.label: Tailscale
reaches.desc: Tailscale Funnel: the box dials OUT to Tailscale (a company); free https://selfprivacy.<tailnet>.ts.net, one hostname, CGNAT-proof.

reaches.label: Cloudflare
reaches.desc: Cloudflare Tunnel: the box dials OUT to Cloudflare (a company); a bought domain (named tunnel, all 5 subdomains) or a free random *.trycloudflare.com (one hostname).

reaches.label: Direct IPv6
reaches.desc: Direct IPv6: friends connect straight to the box's public IPv6 (AAAA record) — no relay, no port-forward; IPv4-only friends can't reach it.

reaches.label: Port-forward
reaches.desc: Port-forward: open TCP 443 on your router to the box by hand + A records to your public IPv4 (needs router admin; dead behind CGNAT).

reaches.label: .onion
reaches.desc: Tor onion service: always on, no company, no domain; friends need a Tor-capable client.

names.label: Buy a domain
names.desc: a domain you buy at a registrar (€/yr); full api./cloud./git./matrix./meet. stack

names.label: Free *.trycloudflare.com
names.desc: a free random *.trycloudflare.com name from a Cloudflare quick tunnel (testing only, changes on restart)

tests.name: onion URL routing
tests.desc: Unit-tests the API logic that rewrites service URLs for .onion path-routing (T1.1–T1.17).
tests.run:
# Pure unit test — no setup, no reach, no network, no box.
./dash run L1.onion-routing
# raw: cd selfprivacy-api && nix run .#pytest-vm -- tests/test_onion_routing.py -q

tests.name: backend up + routing
tests.desc: Boots a NixOS backend in a VM and checks the API + nginx path routing are reachable over the transport (T2/T3).
tests.run:
# L2 integration: boots a throwaway NixOS backend test-VM (harness setup test-vm) and checks API + nginx
# routing over the transport. No app, no box. tor = the onion route; https = local https (self-signed, in the VM).
./dash run L2.backend --net tor
./dash run L2.backend --net https
# raw: cd selfprivacy-tor-tests && nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.tor-integration --no-link -L
#      cd selfprivacy-tor-tests && nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.https-integration --no-link -L

tests.name: connect to server
tests.desc: [desktop] Open the Server details page and load real server information from the backend over the transport.
tests.run:
# Drive the app against a RUNNING backend. Every arg is required: --on (setup = diagram Install+Network),
# --reach [--name] (diagram Reach+Name) and --net (what the app speaks: tor | chutney | https).
# VM on this computer (fresh VM first: ./dash vm-reset && ./dash run install.vm --on vm && ./dash vm-up):
./dash run L3.connect.desktop --on vm --reach onion --net tor
./dash run L3.connect.desktop --on vm --reach onion --net chutney
./dash run L3.connect.desktop --on vm --reach local --net https
# a box (cable-0a cable-0b cable-0d cable-0c wifi-0a wifi-0d usb-0a usb-0d usb-0c), installed + reach applied first:
./dash run L3.connect.desktop --on <SETUP> --reach onion --net tor --ip <BOX_LAN_IP> --key <SSH_KEY> --token <API_TOKEN>
./dash run L3.connect.desktop --on <SETUP> --reach cloudflare --name buy --net https --ip <BOX_LAN_IP> --key <SSH_KEY> --token <API_TOKEN>
./dash run L3.connect.desktop --on <SETUP> --reach ipv6 --name <buy|duckdns> --net https --ip <BOX_LAN_IP> --key <SSH_KEY> --token <API_TOKEN>
./dash run L3.connect.desktop --on <SETUP> --reach portfwd --name <buy|duckdns> --net https --ip <BOX_LAN_IP> --key <SSH_KEY> --token <API_TOKEN>
# (tailscale / cloudflare trycf: one-hostname tunnels, L3 not wired yet — ./dash app --domain <host> --token <API_TOKEN> --apex)

installs.name: LAN cable (netboot over a direct cable)
installs.desc: ONE command per network variant (run install.cable-0a / -0b / -0d / -0c): auto-starts the direct-cable netboot server (one sudo prompt), waits for you to power the target into IPv4 PXE, wipes+installs via nixos-anywhere (no reboot — network-boot-first would loop back into the installer), then verifies the install ON DISK. A live service verify needs the box on its final network: move it to router R (and wifi for 0b/0c/0d), power-cycle, then run the verifier. Installer IP 192.168.100.50.
installs.run:
# FULL end-to-end: wipe target disks -> install SelfPrivacy (NixOS) -> verify. Pick the network variant in the id.
# dash runs a PREFLIGHT for the setup first and refuses with instructions if it isn't ready.
./dash run install.cable-0a --on cable-0a --ip 192.168.100.50 --key <SSH_KEY> \
  --env NETBOOT=auto --env TRANSPORT=<none|https|onion> --env FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> \
  --env MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> --env DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN>
# cable-0b / cable-0d / cable-0c leave the server on wifi: add --env WIFI_SSID=<SSID> --env WIFI_PSK=<PASSWORD>
./dash run install.cable-0d --on cable-0d --ip 192.168.100.50 --key <SSH_KEY> \
  --env NETBOOT=auto --env TRANSPORT=<none|https|onion> --env FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> \
  --env MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> --env DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN> --env WIFI_SSID=<SSID> --env WIFI_PSK=<PASSWORD>
installs.cmd_template: ./dash run install.{setup} --on {setup} --ip 192.168.100.50 --key <SSH_KEY> --env NETBOOT=auto --env TRANSPORT=<none|https|onion> --env FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> --env MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> --env DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN>{wifi}

installs.name: Wifi (netboot through router R)
installs.desc: Your computer on R's wifi, the server netboots through router R (run install.wifi-0a = server cabled to R, install.wifi-0d = server on R's wifi). NOT runnable yet: it needs R configured for network boot and dash has no check for that, so the preflight always refuses (with the setup instructions).
installs.run:
# Needs router R configured for network boot (preflight refuses with instructions otherwise).
./dash run install.wifi-0a --on wifi-0a --ip <TARGET_IP_ON_R> --key <SSH_KEY> \
  --env NETBOOT=off --env TRANSPORT=<https|onion> --env FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> \
  --env MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> --env DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN>
./dash run install.wifi-0d --on wifi-0d --ip <TARGET_IP_ON_R> --key <SSH_KEY> \
  --env NETBOOT=off --env TRANSPORT=<https|onion> --env FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> \
  --env MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> --env DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN> --env WIFI_SSID=<SSID> --env WIFI_PSK=<PASSWORD>
installs.cmd_template: ./dash run install.{setup} --on {setup} --ip <TARGET_IP_ON_R> --key <SSH_KEY> --env NETBOOT=off --env TRANSPORT=<https|onion> --env FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> --env MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> --env DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN>{wifi}

installs.name: USB stick (installer USB → internal disk)
installs.desc: ONE chain per network variant (run install.usb-0a / -0d / -0c): prepare a bootable installer USB on this computer -> you boot+install it on the target -> stamp + verify. Prompts guide the manual steps.
installs.run:
# ONE-CHAIN usb install+verify (prompts for writing the USB and confirming the target install):
./dash run install.usb-0a --on usb-0a --ip <TARGET_IP_ON_R> --key <SSH_KEY> \
  --env USB_DEV=<USB_DEVICE_eg_/dev/sdX> --env TRANSPORT=<none|https|onion> --env FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> \
  --env MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> --env DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN>
# usb-0d / usb-0c leave the server on wifi: add --env WIFI_SSID=<SSID> (checked in range). The USB chain
# writes no wifi config: set the server's wifi up by hand during the USB install.
installs.cmd_template: ./dash run install.{setup} --on {setup} --ip <TARGET_IP_ON_R> --key <SSH_KEY> --env USB_DEV=<USB_DEVICE> --env TRANSPORT=<none|https|onion> --env FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> --env MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> --env DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN>{wifi}

installs.name: VM (VirtualBox on this computer)
installs.desc: NixOS backend in VirtualBox on THIS computer: destroys any old VM and builds the image FROM SOURCE (the committed backend flake), so the VM runs the code under test. 4096 MiB RAM: the in-VM nixos-install livelocked a 2048 MiB guest. Then ./dash vm-up restarts it with the stable VirtualBox settings.
installs.run:
# Fresh VM from source on THIS computer (destroys the old VM), then start it with the stable VirtualBox
# settings and wait for its .onion. VirtualBox must not share VT-x with a running L1/L2.
./dash vm-reset && ./dash run install.vm --on vm && ./dash vm-up
# raw: cd Manager-Ubuntu-SelfPrivacy-Over-Tor/backend && SP_BUILD_MODE=build SP_VM_ACTION=reinstall SP_VM_MEMORY=4096 ./build-and-run.sh
